analysis.scope: SALES-LT-07 and account farah (SSO, mail and CRM sessions); C2 at 203.0.113.45 / cdn-sync-update.example

findings.summary: SALES-LT-07 ran an unsigned installer (PDFEditorSetup.exe) downloaded from pdf-editor-free.example, which started an unsigned svchost-update.exe from AppData\Roaming\SyncUpdate.
svchost-update.exe read the Chrome password and cookie stores (EDR rule CRED-BROWSER-READ): farah's saved credentials and session cookies must be treated as stolen.
A 2.4 MB archive (b7.zip) was staged and uploaded to 203.0.113.45, resolved from cdn-sync-update.example.
Persistence was set through the HKCU Run key 'SyncUpdate' and the host kept beaconing to 203.0.113.45 until 08:12 on 5 Oct: the infection is still active.
farah holds an SSO session and a CRM session (crm-s-7731) opened from SALES-LT-07 before the theft; the CRM stores customer data.
Activity on MKT-LT-11 (aina) and HR-LT-02 (daniel) is signed, routine software and is not linked to this incident.

missing_evidence: Hash reputation/sandbox verdicts for PDFEditorSetup.exe (e18c80a7…) and svchost-update.exe (0387e063…) and whether either is known-bad in threat intel
Full process tree and any additional child processes or dropped files beyond b7.zip, plus memory image of SALES-LT-07 before remediation
Confirmation of what exactly was in the 2.4 MB upload (b7.zip contents) and whether it included CRM/mail session cookies or customer records
Ownership/registration of 203.0.113.45, 203.0.113.10, cdn-sync-update.example and pdf-editor-free.example, and any proxy/DNS logs showing other internal hosts resolving them

Attribution of the 2026-10-05 07:58 SSO sign-in from 192.0.2.61 (state links it to account aina / MKT-LT-11) — confirm whether it is unrelated or a post-compromise access, and review farah's CRM/mail audit logs from 2026-10-04 21:42 onward for use of the stolen session
Whether the download was user-initiated via search/advertisement or delivered through an email/message (no phishing artefact in this batch)
Any change-management record that could explain the download/installation on SALES-LT-07

actions.rationale: Capture volatile and stored artifacts from SALES-LT-07 before any remediation or reimage to support investigation, confirm scope, and preserve potential legal/HR evidence. Include process tree, memory, browser artifacts, network connections, and dropped files.
prerequisites: EDR live-response channel to SALES-LT-07 is available
actions.risk: Low: read-only collection; adds a short delay before re-imaging.
actions.expected_effect: Memory and disk images of SALES-LT-07 captured with a chain-of-custody record.

actions.rationale: Evidence shows an unsigned installer (PDFEditorSetup.exe → svchost-update.exe) on SALES-LT-07 accessed the browser credential store and uploaded 2.4 MB to 203.0.113.45. Isolating the host stops further credential access, exfiltration, and potential lateral movement. POL-04 allows a SOC analyst to approve isolating a user laptop alone.
actions.risk: Farah loses network access on SALES-LT-07 until release.
actions.expected_effect: SALES-LT-07 network-contained; only the EDR management channel remains.
validation_checks: No further connections from SALES-LT-07 to 203.0.113.45
EDR reports the host as contained

actions.rationale: The infostealer accessed the browser credential store on SALES-LT-07, placing account farah's credentials and potentially active session tokens at risk. Revoking active sessions invalidates any stolen tokens and forces re-authentication. POL-07 permits a SOC analyst to approve revoking sessions for a compromised account alone.
actions.risk: Farah is signed out of SSO, mail and CRM.
actions.expected_effect: All active sessions for farah invalidated in idp, mail and crm.

actions.rationale: Stolen browser credentials require a password reset to prevent account takeover and downstream access to mail, SSO, and other services. POL-07 permits a SOC analyst to approve resetting the password of a compromised account alone.
prerequisites: User available for a user-assisted reset
actions.risk: Requires Farah to set a new password; existing sessions stay valid until revoked.
actions.expected_effect: The stolen password no longer authenticates.
validation_checks: Password sign-ins with the old credential fail

actions.rationale: svchost-update.exe resolved cdn-sync-update.example to 203.0.113.45, uploaded the staged archive there and kept beaconing. Blocking the domain cuts the command-and-control and exfiltration channel for any other infected host.
actions.risk: Low: the domain has no business use.
actions.expected_effect: cdn-sync-update.example sinkholed at the resolver and blocked at the web proxy.
validation_checks: DNS queries for the domain return the sinkhole

actions.rationale: pdf-editor-free.example served the unsigned installer that started the infection. Blocking it stops other staff downloading the same payload.
actions.expected_effect: pdf-editor-free.example blocked at the resolver and web proxy.
validation_checks: Proxy blocks requests to the domain

analysis.scope: Account farah and CRM customer data; SALES-LT-07 contained; attacker at 198.51.100.23

findings.summary: farah's stolen CRM session crm-s-7731 was replayed from 198.51.100.23 on a new device fingerprint at 10:20, after the IdP session had been revoked.
The replayed session exported 1,200 customer records (name, phone, email, company) and downloaded export_customers_central.csv.
The earlier session revocation failed in the CRM during vendor maintenance; the CRM admin API is available again.
Farah was in a client meeting from 10:00 and has not used the CRM today: the 10:20 CRM activity is the attacker.
SALES-LT-07 is contained: its outbound connection to 203.0.113.45 was dropped.

missing_evidence: CRM admin API is back online (vendor maintenance ended 10:30) — revoke remaining CRM session crm-s-7731 and confirm no other live sessions for farah.
Full inventory of credentials and cookies stolen from farah's browser stores (which additional apps/accounts the stolen cookies can still access).
Complete CRM audit trail of the attacker session crm-s-7731 (all views, exports, changes, and any further downloads beyond export_customers_central.csv).

Verification whether the SSO sign-ins from 192.0.2.61 at 2026-10-05 07:58 and 09:30 and the CRM sign-in crm-s-8120 at 10:05 were the legitimate user or the attacker (user reported being in a meeting from 10:00).
Sweep for the same installer binary/hash (PDFEditorSetup.exe, svchost-update.exe) or related C2 (203.0.113.45, cdn-sync-update.example, pdf-editor-free.example) on other endpoints and accounts.
Malware/C2 analysis of the dropped binary and staging archive to confirm stealer family and any secondary payloads or lateral movement.
Ownership/registration verification of pdf-editor-free.example, cdn-sync-update.example and 203.0.113.45.

actions.rationale: The stolen CRM session crm-s-7731 was replayed from 198.51.100.23 and used to export 1,200 customer records. The first revocation failed in the CRM during vendor maintenance; the admin API is back, so revoking again closes the attacker's live session. POL-07 permits a SOC analyst to approve revoking sessions alone.
actions.risk: Farah is signed out of every service again.
actions.expected_effect: Active sessions for farah revoked in idp, mail and crm, including crm-s-7731.

actions.rationale: The attacker holds farah's stolen browser credentials and is actively trying to sign in from 198.51.100.23. Disabling the account blocks new sign-ins until a user-assisted reset is done. POL-02 requires IT-manager approval to disable a staff account.
actions.risk: Farah cannot work until the account is re-enabled.
actions.expected_effect: New sign-ins for farah are blocked at the identity provider.
validation_checks: Sign-in attempts for farah are rejected as disabled
